Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free. “No, there’s no toll at all. It is for them; they are the ones using it. We are just making it a standard park that we will replicate all over the state as time goes on,” he said. On the management of the facility after completion, Giwa said it would remain the property of the Lagos State Government under the supervision of the Ministry of Transportation. He added that the government was working with transport unions to ensure effective utilisation of the facility and prevent its takeover by miscreants. Giwa also warned commercial bus drivers against picking up passengers or parking along road corridors outside the designated terminal after its opening. He said the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) would enforce compliance with traffic regulations. “By the time we finish this place, there will be no need for us to have any bus on the road, and Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, will be on the ground to ensure they comply with all the rules and regulations of Lagos State. “The laws are there. She said the facility would follow the model of the JJT Park in Alausa and remain open to the public free of charge for everyday recreational activities. However, corporate organisations and other groups seeking to organise formal events or competitions at the venue would be required to pay a nominal maintenance fee, she added. Construction resumed in mid-October, with clearing, foundation work and material deliveries, while interlocking pavement, curbing and fencing works were ongoing as of mid-November. The wider redevelopment plan also includes electric vehicle charging points, more than 60 public toilet fixtures, a recycling drop-off station, kiosks and commercial spaces, solar lighting and tree planting. Other components include a Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) road camp for street sweepers and security personnel, improved lighting and CCTV facilities, as well as maintenance arrangements for the park and adjoining Macgregor Canal. Anyaehie gave the charge on Thursday in Awka while delivering his address at the university’s 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies. He urged the graduands to become worthy ambassadors of the institution, named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa. Expounding on the university’s motto, the Vice-Chancellor said discipline required the graduands to make integrity, self-control and ethical conduct their guiding principles in an increasingly complex world. On self-reliance, he advised them not to wait for opportunities to come their way but to embrace innovation, create value, build enterprises and develop solutions to real-life challenges. He also urged them to pursue excellence and reject mediocrity, stressing that every task they undertook should reflect world-class standards. item.title: Afreximbank provides $30 m to finance Nigerian SME exports through NEXIM
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs). The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM). “The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay. The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said. It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos. “Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying. “By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added. Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said, “We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.” The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support. CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts

item.title: ‘Obi Will Disgrace Him Spectacularly In Anambra,’ Momodu Dismisses Soludo’s Victory Promise For Tinubu

On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election. “The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. item.title: 2027: PDP insists on coalition to challenge Nwifuru in Ebonyi
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has insisted that a coalition of political parties and interest groups exists to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of Governor Francis Nwifuru in the 2027 governorship election. The party said the APC’s claim that it was not part of any coalition did not invalidate the existence of political groups working together to challenge the incumbent administration. The media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr Ifeanyichukwu Odii, Dr Jerry Uhuo, stated this while reacting to comments by the APC campaign spokesman, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, who had alleged that no coalition existed in Ebonyi State. Uhuo accused Onwe of misunderstanding the concept of political coalition, explaining that it involved political interest groups coming together to pursue common objectives, including electoral victory. “From all indications, Sen. Onwe appears not to understand what coalition means in the context of the current political engineering. “Coalition is a coming together of political interest groups to work together for the interest of promoting a common interest and winning election. “The fact that the Ebonyi APC claims non-membership of such a coalition does not mean that the coalition does not exist in Ebonyi. He admitted that any group could come together to form a coalition. That alone contradicts his original position,” he said. Uhuo argued that the formation of a political coalition did not require the endorsement of a state government, insisting that political parties and interest groups were free to collaborate. He added that the PDP and other political groups were already working together to challenge the APC-led administration in the state ahead of the 2027 elections. “In the case of Ebonyi, the PDP and other political groups are already working together to dislodge the government of Governor Francis Nwifuru,” he stated. item.title: 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger
item.description: NO fewer than 14 persons reportedly lost their lives in a road accident involving a DAF truck conveying 35 cattle and several passengers along Kontagora Road in Niger State. Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, reported that the accident occurred around 11 a.m. on November 17 near Ibeto, as the truck, with registration number Lagos AZL 267 XH, travelled from Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State to Lagos. “Police sources said an unidentified vehicle travelling in the same direction reportedly attempted to overtake the truck but brushed against it, causing the driver to lose control before the vehicle fell,” Makama said. “The truck driver and 13 other occupants reportedly died at the scene. “Those identified among the deceased included Umar, 45, the driver, from Kaoje; Anas Suleiman, 25, and Sufiyanu Suleiman, 40, both from Koko; Salim Abu Dogo, 30; Abubakar Shehu, 45; Yahaya Abubakar, 30; and Manu, 35, all from Dankigari. “Others were Rufai Umar, 25, from Bagudo; Faruk Tudu Kaoje, 20, from Kaoje; Umar Abubakar, 30, from Saradosa; Salisu Idry, 35, from Bagodo; and Abubakar Alhaji, 25, from Kaoje.” Police sources told Makama that relatives identified the bodies, while those claimed by their families were released for burial in accordance with Islamic rites. The publication added that two unidentified bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of Kontagora General Hospital. “The vehicle allegedly involved in the overtaking manoeuvre was later traced to Kaboji in Magama Local Government Area and taken to the Area Command Office,” Makama said. “However, the driver of the vehicle reportedly fled and remains at large.” According to the publication, the Niger State Police Command said investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the accident and apprehend the fleeing driver. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” Shettima said. ‎ ‎He described Buhari’s Spartan lifestyle as remarkable in a political environment where public office is sometimes pursued to satisfy private interests. ‎ ‎”His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. There was something arresting about a man who could command so much and desire so little,” he stated. ‎ ‎Shettima noted that Buhari’s political journey, spanning military leadership and democratic governance, attracted both extraordinary public affection and strong criticism over his policies and decisions. ‎ ‎He, however, said the former President’s enduring connection with millions of Nigerians reflected a distinctive leadership disposition that defied conventional political calculations. ‎ ‎Beyond the tribute, the Vice President described the biography as an important contribution to historical documentation, institutional memory and public accountability. ‎ ‎He urged serving public officials to preserve records of their decisions and explain the circumstances surrounding them, warning that failure to do so could leave future generations vulnerable to speculation and distorted accounts of national events. ‎ ‎”The privilege of serving a nation includes the obligation of explanation. History becomes poorer whenever those who could have supplied its evidence leave it with unanswered questions,” he said. ‎ ‎Shettima commended Buhari for authorising the biographical project during his lifetime and participating in the research, noting that his recollections, alongside interviews and documentary evidence, would enrich the historical record. ‎ ‎In his remarks, Issoufou, who chaired the occasion, said the publication provided an opportunity to move beyond mourning and subject Buhari’s life and leadership to objective historical reflection. ‎ ‎He described the three-volume work as a significant contribution to Nigeria’s historical record, particularly for younger generations who did not have personal encounters with the former President. ‎ ‎”Today, in presenting these volumes, we move from mourning to historical reflection. Mourning belongs first to the family, friends and contemporaries. History belongs to everyone, including generations that never knew the man,” he said. ‎ ‎Issoufou cautioned against presenting Buhari’s legacy in absolute terms, insisting that a fair historical assessment must accommodate both his accomplishments and shortcomings. ‎ ‎”None of us can claim to have the final word on Muhammadu Buhari. Nor should any biography pretend to do so,” he added. ‎ ‎Former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, who represented former President Goodluck Jonathan, also recalled Buhari’s commitment to personal relationships, describing it as an important aspect of his character that deserved recognition. ‎ ‎Earlier, the author, Dr Udu Yakubu, said the three-volume biography was the culmination of more than two and a half years of research, interviews and documentation. ‎ ‎He acknowledged Buhari’s cooperation throughout the process, noting that the former President granted him access to relevant information without compromising his independence as a researcher. ‎ ‎”He gave the work the legitimacy of access without taking away my independence of judgement. I regret that he did not live to see these works completed, but the record now carries his voice,” Yakubu said. ‎ ‎Reviewing the first volume, “Buhari: The Phenomenon”, Ambassador Dr Chijioke Wigwe described it as an authoritative account of the former President’s life, containing some of his final substantial recorded reflections. ‎ ‎He traced Buhari’s journey from his upbringing in Daura, Katsina State, through his military career and appointment as Federal Commissioner for Petroleum Resources to his emergence as Head of State and eventual return to farming after leaving office. ‎ ‎Wigwe observed that Buhari’s firm and uncompromising disposition shaped his leadership and influenced the circumstances surrounding his removal from power. ‎ ‎He said the biography offered an opportunity to examine Buhari’s character and place in Nigeria’s history without sentiment or prejudice. ‎ ‎”History must neither flatter nor condemn blindly but must examine dispassionately the human being whose life became part of the Nigerian story,” he said. ‎ ‎Also reviewing the second and third volumes, The Presidency and “The Reckoning”, Ambassador Professor Tijjani Muhammad-Bande identified institutional discipline, accountability and national unity as defining features of Buhari’s leadership. ‎ ‎He recalled the former President’s insistence that public funds spent on government projects must translate into tangible results, as well as his respect for institutional procedures and the constitutional tenure of public officeholders. ‎ ‎Muhammad-Bande further described Buhari as a committed believer in Nigeria’s unity who opposed violent attempts to undermine the country’s territorial integrity. ‎ ‎He said Buhari recognised the constitutional right to peaceful protest but maintained a firm position against taking up arms against the Nigerian state, regarding national unity as a responsibility that transcended ethnic, religious and political divisions. ‎ ‎The three-volume biography examines Buhari’s personal background, military career, political journey and eight-year presidency, providing a historical account of a leader whose legacy continues to attract debate across Nigeria. item.title: Yiaga Africa Urges INEC To Publish Guidelines For Nov. 28 Mock Accreditation
item.description: Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28. The organisation said timely access to information about the exercise was necessary to enable citizens, political parties, civil society organisations, election observers, and the media to understand, participate in, and monitor the process. In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Samson Itodo, Yiaga Africa welcomed INEC’s decision to conduct the exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections. It said the exercise was consistent with sustained calls by citizens and civil society organisations for the commission to adequately test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) before the elections. COMBO: Photo of YIAGA Africa executive director Samson Itodo and INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan “However, Yiaga Africa is concerned that, despite the importance of the exercise, the Commission is yet to make public comprehensive guidelines and a framework outlining how it will be conducted. The list of polling units where the exercise will take place is also yet to be made public. “For an exercise of this significance, timely access to information is essential. Citizens and electoral stakeholders should have sufficient information and notice to understand, participate in, and observe the process,” the statement read in part. Yiaga Africa said transparency in the exercise would be crucial to building public confidence in the electoral technologies that would be deployed for the 2027 elections. It called on INEC to immediately publish a comprehensive framework outlining the scope, modalities and procedures for the exercise. The organisation also urged the commission to release the complete list of participating polling units and other relevant locations early enough to give stakeholders sufficient time to prepare for the exercise. Yiaga Africa further urged INEC to use the mock exercise as an opportunity to demonstrate transparency and responsiveness while allowing meaningful public scrutiny of BVAS and IReV. The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and take place across all states of the federation. He said the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. The 2027 Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will be held on February 6. item.title: When Ndigbo Become President, It Must Be Eight Full Years — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the South-East should have a full eight-year presidential tenure when a candidate from the region eventually becomes Nigeria’s president. Oshiomhole also praised Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo, a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), for his economic expertise and leadership. ﻿ He said Soludo understood the challenges facing Nigeria’s economy, particularly the disconnect between monetary and fiscal policies. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. It further observed that countries with operational instant payment systems record approximately seven percentage points higher active account usage.
